trust_decision.summary: Read-only mode is decided twice: per request at the MCP tool gate, where execute_sql splits the batch on ';' and asks isReadOnlySQL about each statement, and (after this fix) per execution inside each connector's executeSQL, where the database engine itself must reject the write. At the pinned commit the second decision does not exist, so a statement the keyword classifier mis-parses reaches the engine and is executed.

landing_point.why: The advisory summary names read-only mode, and this is the only read-only gate applied to user SQL; an engineer starts here, then follows it into isReadOnlySQL in src/utils/allowed-keywords.ts.

O3_reason_to_dismiss: SQL Server is an optional driver whose engine has no READ ONLY transaction, and the project's own docs call read-only 'a safety net ... not a security boundary' (docs/tools/execute-sql.mdx:129), so the missing engine backstop there can be argued never to have been covered.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: A non-read-only tool call on the same shared connection must stay writable after a read-only call (SQLite keeps one `this.db` for every tool, MySQL/MariaDB take one pooled connection per call), and legitimate read-only introspection pragmas must keep passing: sqlite allows the `pragma` keyword (src/utils/allowed-keywords.ts:13), the connector treats `pragma` + table_info/index_info/index_list/foreign_key_list as a read statement (src/connectors/sqlite/index.ts:468-472), and the pinned unit test asserts `PRAGMA table_info(users)` is read-only (src/utils/__tests__/allowed-keywords.test.ts:62-63). An over-broad fix that opens the database read-only, always sets a session read-only flag, or rejects every parenthesised/`=` pragma breaks one of these.

O6_input_shapes: single statement vs a ';'-joined multi-statement batch
SQLite `PRAGMA name = value` and the no-space `PRAGMA name=value`
SQLite parenthesised setter alias `PRAGMA name(value)` (and `schema.name(...)`) which SQLite treats like `=`
MySQL/MariaDB `--` followed by a non-space, e.g. `SELECT 1--1;DROP TABLE t` — two minus operators, not a comment
MySQL/MariaDB `--` followed by whitespace or a control char (0x7F) — a real comment that swallows the rest of the line
function-based writes that begin with an allowed keyword, e.g. `SELECT setval(pg_get_serial_sequence(...), 1, true)`
in-batch state toggles: `PRAGMA query_only = OFF; INSERT ...` / `PRAGMA query_only(0)`
per-dialect difference: `--` is always a comment for postgres/sqlite/sqlserver, conditional for mysql/mariadb
MySQL conditional comments `/*! ... */` and `/*M! ... */` stay executable text

O8_uncovered_routes.route: SQL Server executeSQL has no engine-level backstop at all: a read-only execute_sql tool on a sqlserver source is protected only by the keyword classifier, and the published fix did not touch this connector.
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: T-SQL has no READ ONLY transaction; the connector is an optional driver (mssql) and the fix's own comments scope the backstop to the four dialects it patched, while the docs say read-only is a keyword safety net, not a security boundary.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: src/tools/execute-sql.ts -> src/connectors/sqlserver/index.ts (separate connector package, untouched by the fix)

O8_uncovered_routes.route: Custom tools check `readonly` with isReadOnlySQL over the whole statement and never split on ';', so a stacked `SELECT 1; DROP TABLE t` statement passes the gate for every dialect (the execute_sql gate splits first).
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: The statement is operator-authored TOML configuration, not request input, and its parameters are bound, so the route is 'not attacker controlled'.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: sibling handler in the same tools package, check re-exported at src/utils/tool-handler-helpers.ts:36

O8b_injection_room.sibling: The same per-execution engine backstop the fix added to the other four connectors (a READ ONLY transaction or an equivalent session guard).
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The SQL Server connector already implements executeSQL and EXPLAIN translation in the same shape as the postgres/mysql connectors; a maintainer adding a per-tool read-only backstop would naturally add it here too.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A second execution path (explainQuery: SET SHOWPLAN_XML ON, then request.query on the inner statement) that a guard placed in executeSQL would not cover.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: EXPLAIN is translated into its own private path with its own session handling, so hardening executeSQL alone leaves it out — exactly the shape of a how-type sibling.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: Per-statement splitting (areAllStatementsReadOnly, src/tools/execute-sql.ts:26-29) instead of the whole-string isReadOnlySQL.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The two read-only gates were written independently; a maintainer fixing the batch bypass would plausibly copy the splitter into the custom-tool handler.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: Connection-level enforcement (default_transaction_read_only, and SQLite's read-only open at src/connectors/sqlite/index.ts:192) duplicating the per-execution route.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: That wider route already exists at the pinned commit and is the obvious place a maintainer would extend instead of adding a per-call transaction.

O9_family: CWE-184 / CWE-636 / CWE-863: an incomplete keyword blacklist used as an authorization check for read-only mode, with no fail-safe enforcement below it
